data.name: Vickie
data.gender_notes: Vickie is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word ‘victoria’, meaning ‘victory’. This name was popularized by the Roman goddess Victoria, who symbolized triumph and victory. The name Vickie carries the meaning “Victory” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Vickie usually hope their child will grow to embody victory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the spirit of victory in life.
data.etymology: Vickie belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vickie total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vickie gained popularity in the English-speaking world during the nineteenth century as a freed slaves' name in the United States. It was also among the favorites of the suffrage movement during the early twentieth century, inspiring women to strive for victory in their pursuit of equality. Today, the name evokes a sense of strength, resilience, and determination, fitting for individuals who have faced adversity and come out victorious.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Vickie holds spiritual significance as a reminder of the ultimate victory that comes from faith in Jesus Christ. As 1 Corinthians 15:57 says, "But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ." The name echoes the themes of triumph, strength, and hope found in the Bible, inspiring those who bear it to live with faith and perseverance in their daily lives.
